steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Sift flour, salt, cinnamon, baking soda, and nutmeg together into a bowl.
Beat sugar and shortening together in a separate large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Add oatmeal, banana, nuts, and egg; beat well. Add in flour mixture; mix well.
Drop teaspoonfuls of dough onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges turn lightly brown, about 15 minutes. Cool on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Oatmeal Cookie
raw_recipe.description: This recipe has been handed down in my family for generations. It's a good way to use overripe bananas. It's also a moist cookie that travels well either in the mail or car.
raw_recipe.name: Banana Oatmeal Cookie

review.reviewBody: I made these twice so far. The first time I omitted the nuts, added a bit more cinnamon, they turned out great, they stay soft forever. The second time I added dried cranberries and everyone at work loved them! I keep a sheet of foil a rack below the cookies so they don't burn on the bottom, as they have a longer cook time (15 mins was perfect). I'll definitely make these again.

Okay...the first batch, following the original recipe was okay, but didn't really have the oatmeal cookie texture I was looking for and they were just a tad bland. So I made some tweaks and the second batch was perfect! Here are my tweaks: I used room temp butter instead of shortening, I increased the cinnamon to 1 1/2 tsp, I used 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar, added 1 tsp. vanilla (because why not?) and increased the oats to 3 cups. And because I'm a chocoholic I added 1/2 cup mini chocolate chips. Baked at 350° for 12 minutes. Perfection! Everyone loved them!

I also omitted the nuts and increased the cinnamon to a full teaspoon. My first batch burned at 400 degrees for 15 minutes, so I reduced the oven temp to 350 degrees and baked for 12 minutes, and they were perfect. To increase the banana flavor, refrigerate the whole bowl of cookie dough for 30 minutes or so before baking. Return unused dough to the refrigerator between batches. That will also help keep the cookies from spreading too thin while baking. I like this recipe and will keep it for the next time I have leftover ripe bananas. I added 1/2 cup dried cherries to second half of cookie dough, and they were even better!

Just tried this today to use up some ripe bananas. I did add extra cinnamon and had to use steel cut oatmeal as I had none of the regular oatmeal. I just let the batter set awhile so the oatmeal would soften some; it gave the cookies kind of a nutty chewy texture which I love. I left out nuts. 
I also did half brown sugar, half white sugar. Did a second batch adding chocolate chips and craisins.
Dropped the baking time and temperature. Baked at 375 on center rack and checked at 13 minutes as the bottoms were browning well.
 YUM! This will definitely be my go to cookie to use up bananas.

Amazing!! I changed a few things- I used 2/3 cup of sugar, and half butter half coconut oil instead of shortening. I didn't add any nuts, and instead added about half a cup of dark chocolate chips and 1/4 cup shaved coconut. I also took some reviewers advice and cooked mine at 375 for about 15 minutes. They turned out so good! They were even a bit crispy on the outside- that probably won't last overnight, but was amazing right out of the oven.

I make these cookies all the time, my son loves them. And they are sort of healthy - I consider them a health food! I add either raisins or blueberries to mine. And the cook temp is way too high - I do mine at 350 and they come out really soft and chewy. Yum!

Love this recipe! Couple changes though… I used 2 cups of oatmeal instead of 1 3/4 cups, added a half cup of packed brown sugar, doubled the vanilla extract, used 3/4 cup of salted butter instead of shortening, baked on 375 instead of 400 and for 11 minute they came out absolutely perfect my fiancé is eating them all up as I type haha! Thanks for the recipe

I used a stick of butter and 1/4 cup of coconut oil instead of shortening. 1/2 c brown sugar and 1/2 c white sugar. I also used 3/4 c of dried cranberries instead of nuts. I made 30 cookies but could have done 36 if I paid more attention to portioning. There was some spread when they baked, but if you leave them as a sizable dollop, they will come out thick in the center. Definitely like muffin tops instead of cookies, but everybody at playdates (moms and kids) love them!

I made it how it was directed but I used flavored instant oats the raisin and spice.. 1/2 tsp of vanilla and extra 1/2 cup of mashed banana and cooked them on 375 for 12 mins.. They were great my kids loves them. My fiance does not like sweet desserts but he ate most of the batch. Thanks ??

I made a few adjustments to this recipe and made it a keeper! I couldn't bring myself to use shortening so I used 3/4 C plus 2 TBS of room temperature butter and refrigerated the dough for a few minutes before scooping/baking it. I also added 1 1/4 C of frozen blueberries. These cookies were delicious!

These cookies are delicious as is, but I wanted less sugar sweetness & more protein. I used 1/2 c olive oil, 2 eggs, 2 mashed bananas and 1 small grated apple, 1 c oatmeal and 1 c cooked quinoa, 1 c white flour and 1/2c white wheat flour. Next time I'll increase the cinnamon to 1 tsp. Great with a hot cup of tea!
I was raised on a very similar cookie recipe. My mother found it in The Agricultualist Magazine in the 1960’s. However, my mother always used real butter. It is also a good use for browning bananas.
Moist and delicious. I did do the half butter half coconut oil suggested by someone else and recommend it!

I didn't read directions, I just mixed all ingredients together at once . I had a roast in the oven so I heated up my waffle iron and cooked on there. Crispy amazing goodness!! Needs a but more cinnamon is only negative.

Fantastic. My new favorite cookie! What a great way to get rid of a couple overripe bananas. I used cashews and was a very nice complimen to the bananas. The banana cookie was fluffy with the cashews adding a crunch factor.

I did not like these cookies. The first batch burned 15 minutes. I cooked the second batch for only 12 minutes and they turned out better. I followed the recipe exactly except I added a half cup of chocolate chips. They were too cakey to me like a muffin. Not like cookies at all and dry. Just so disappointed!
I added dark chocolate chips. Made them even better 😁r
I could not do the nuts, first batch was scrumptious 2nd batch added 1/2c. coconut and1/2c. blueberries. great recipe.
